name: t1
description: Observaki T1 reference benchmark cluster. The minimum topology that can sustain the 1M events/s reference workload and cover the G1 throughput and query baselines with 7 days of hot retention. The profile is provider-neutral; the AWS Terraform module is the reference implementation.

roles.name: clickhouse
roles.purpose: Logs and traces storage/query. 32 TiB raw per node; replication 2 leaves 96 TiB logical, enough for 7 days at 1M events/s with headroom.

roles.name: victoriametrics
roles.purpose: Metrics and RED storage. 12 TiB raw per node; replication 2 leaves 18 TiB logical for the 60% metrics share.

roles.name: gateway
roles.purpose: OTLP ingest, RED calculation and WAL client. Six nodes give 1.44M events/s at the conservative 15k events/s per vCPU target; NFR-9 targets less than 8 GiB RSS per gateway.

roles.name: nats
roles.purpose: JetStream WAL with replication 2. 2 TiB raw covers at least one hour of the full workload during an outage.

roles.name: loadgen
roles.purpose: OTLP workload generator. Two hosts run the five shards of throughput-5m; the 1M/s gate uses fewer shards.

notes: The profile sizes the full T1 reference (7 days of hot retention), not just the one-hour throughput run. A shorter retention run uses less disk; the difference must be stated in the report.
The 32 TiB ClickHouse data disk is split into two 16 TiB gp3 volumes because that is the AWS per-volume limit. Other providers can use a single larger volume.

The cluster is deliberately single-AZ for the benchmark: cross-AZ replication and transfer would change both the latency and the cost. Production HA is a separate topology and is not what this profile measures.
The profile does not include a PostgreSQL control plane, object storage, backups or a support plan. Those are production costs, not benchmark costs.
